newsitem.title: UK: Fannie Mae FFR jumbo waiting for launch.
newsitem.headline: Fannie Mae FFR jumbo waiting for launch.

text.p: The long-awaited French franc jumbo Eurobond for the U.S. national mortgage association Fannie Mae will be launched as soon as an opportunity arises in the swap markets, a syndicate manager at Societe Generale said.
"Its impossible to reach Fannie Mae's funding targets at the current swap levels," the syndicate manager told Reuters.
"If market conditions allow us to reach Fannie Mae's target its likely that Merrill Lynch and Societe Generale will be mandated to launch an issue," he added.
Societe Generale and Merrill Lynch are tipped as favourites for joint lead managers of the transaction following the investor presentations it organised for the borrower in November last year.
The offering is expected to be for between 3.0 and 5.0 billion French francs at a 10 to 12 year maturity.
Market sources said at a 12 year maturity, a spread of around 14 basis points over French government paper was likely while at a 10 year maturity, a spread of 12 b.p. over was likely.
But the Societe Generale syndicate manager said the maturity was flexible and could even be for five years if that was the best window of opportunity.
"We have to find the best compromise between the swaps level and the demand."
He said although the French institutional investors were cash rich, they were reluctant to invest at current levels and were waiting for the market to consolidate.
He said March and April were good months for launch as there was a lot of French franc redemptions due.
He said the deal could have a clause enabling the paper to be paid in euros when the single currency comes into effect as the recent Hydro Quebec French franc issue had.

This clause stated: "Interest and payment of principal will be considered as denominated and payable in euros if the French franc is replaced by the euro." -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
